chunks: And through this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, who said: Ali ibn Sulayman al-Zarari narrated to us, from Ali ibn Sadaqah al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him), who said:

A letter came to Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him) spontaneously, without any prior inquiry, instructing him to inform those who ask about the Name: either remain silent and attain Paradise, or speak and be condemned to the Fire. For if they discern the Name, they will spread it, and if they discover the place, they will lead others to it.

key_terms.الاسم: The Name (referring to the Imam's name)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of revealing the Imam's name during the Occultation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Book of Ghaybah instructs Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari to convey a message regarding the secrecy of the Imam's identity. It presents a dichotomy: keeping the Imam's name secret leads to Paradise, while revealing it leads to Hellfire, as knowledge of the name or location would lead to its dissemination.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 331 - Through the same chain of narration from Muhammad Ibn Ali from his father, who said: Ali Ibn Sulaiman Razi recounted to us on the authority of Ali Ibn Sadaqah Qummi, who said:

A letter came to Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari without any inquiry from him and commanded him to inform the people who were inquiring about the name of the Imam to either be silent and attain Paradise or either talk and be condemned to the Fire. For if they discern the name, they will spread it, and if they discover the place, they will lead others to it.
